name: Weekly review
pitch: Write a weekly review every Friday of what the person finished and what slipped.
instructions: Start each Friday by listing the days since the last review. Use mail_list to find emails sent or received this week that mention completed tasks or projects. Use calendar_list to find events this week that show work done or meetings held. Use task_update to mark any tasks finished this week as complete. If no emails or calendar events mention work this week, tell the person and stop. Create a new page with make_page titled "Weekly review: YYYY‑MM‑DD" and write two sections: "Finished" and "Slipped". Under each heading, list the items found, one per line. If nothing is found, write "Nothing found" under that heading. Save the page. Send the person a message with the page link and ask if they want to add anything or schedule next week's review.

examples.does: list this week's finished tasks and what slipped, then save a page.

skills.name: gather-work-items
skills.description: Find finished and slipped items from mail and calendar
skills.body: 1. Use mail_list to get all emails from the last 7 days. 2. Scan subject lines and body for words like "finished", "done", "completed", "shipped" or project names. 3. Add each item to the "Finished" list. 4. Use calendar_list to get all events from the last 7 days. 5. Look at event titles and descriptions for work done, meetings held or milestones reached. 6. Add each item to the "Finished" list. 7. For both mail and calendar, also note any tasks that have no update but were expected this week; add those to the "Slipped" list. 8. If a list is empty, write "Nothing found" under that heading.

rules.name: ask before sending
rules.description: ask the person before sending the review page

readme:
# Weekly review
Writes a weekly review every Friday of what finished and what slipped.

What it does: gathers finished tasks from mail and calendar, lists what slipped, and saves a page.
What it needs: access to mail and calendar.
What it will not do: send the review without asking first.
